definition: Consummate means to complete a deal, agreement, or marriage by carrying out its final, binding step.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word consummate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know consummate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After a year of talks, the two railway companies finally consummated their merger at Friday's signing.
Settle is looser and weaker — parties can settle on terms informally over a handshake; to consummate a deal is to carry it all the way to full, formal completion.
Ratify is even more formal than consummate: it adds an official vote or seal of approval by a governing body, not just the parties themselves.

Finalize means to complete the last step of something - you finalize plans, a schedule, or a design. Consummate is narrower and more formal: it applies to deals, agreements, and marriages, where one final binding act seals the arrangement. Everyday things get finalized; a merger gets consummated.

Complete means to bring something to an end - the most general word for finishing anything at all. Consummate is reserved for a specific kind of finishing: carrying out the final, binding step that seals a deal, agreement, or marriage. Any task can be completed; only a formal arrangement between parties is consummated.
to give up on entirely
to break an arrangement apart

Consummate means to complete a deal, agreement, or marriage by carrying out its final, binding step.
The two rival orchards had circled each other for three seasons.
Their lawyers exchanged drafts; their owners haggled over water rights and the fate of the old cider press.
Twice the talks collapsed entirely.
Then, on a rainy Tuesday, both families sat at the same kitchen table and signed every page.
The partnership so many had doubted was finally consummated.
The signing that turns years of drafts and negotiations into a finished, binding partnership shows what it means to consummate an agreement.
formal; business and legal contexts
In this unit, consummate is the verb (kon-suh-MAYT): to complete a deal, agreement, or marriage.
Watch out for the unrelated-sounding adjective (kon-SUM-it), as in 'a consummate professional' — that sense means 'supremely skilled' and is not the one being taught here.

For a year, the owner of the Corner Bookshop and the manager of the regional chain circled each other with offers and counteroffers.
By March they had agreed on everything: price, staff, even the fate of the store cat.
Yet nothing was binding, and both sides knew a handshake was not a sale.
The lawyers set the closing for a Tuesday.
To consummate the purchase, the parties met once, signed four documents, and exchanged the keys and the payment in the same hour.
Until that hour, either side could still have walked away.
The chain's newsletter announced the deal that evening — not when the terms were agreed, but when the final binding act had sealed them.
